Do these steps immediately, in order:

1. Stop more water from coming:
   - Look behind or beside the toilet for the SHUTOFF VALVE (small knob on the pipe going into the toilet).
   - Turn it clockwise (to the right) until it stops. If it’s hard, use both hands and keep turning slowly.
   - If you can’t find it, open the toilet tank lid and lift the FLOAT (the plastic ball or cup) straight up and keep it up to stop water refilling. If someone else is home, have them hold it.

2. Kill power if water is near outlets or cords:
   - If water is close to any electrical outlets, power strips, or appliances, go to the breaker panel and switch OFF the breakers for that area before stepping in more water.

3. Contain the water:
   - Use towels, rags, or mops to block doorways so water doesn’t spread to other rooms.
   - If you have a bucket and the toilet is still overflowing, try to catch water coming over the rim so it doesn’t spread.

4. Don’t flush again and don’t use other toilets or drains on the same floor if they’re backing up.

Now I need a bit of info so I can get an emergency plumber to you:

1) Is water still actively coming out of the toilet, or has it stopped?
2) What’s your full address (or at least city + ZIP)?
3) Are any other drains (shower, sink, other toilets) backing up too?
4) Can you safely walk in the area without stepping in deep water or near live outlets?</action>
